body:
## Summary

Fixes #2140.

A `solve --tool codex` run that had **finished its work** — [formal-ai#927](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/927) updated, all 46 check-runs green on the final commit, `turn.completed` received, exit 0 — was declared failed by the completion gate with `turn.started=3, turn.completed=1`, after $179.99 of model spend.

Replaying the real 96,409-line log through the actual parser proves the two extra `turn.started` records arrived on Codex's **stderr**, inside an OTEL `codex.tool_result` dump. This is the [#2136](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2136) defect on a binary released *before* that fix shipped: the run started at 03:58:27Z, the #2136 fix merged at 04:04:52 and released as 2.11.10 at 04:16:33 — the process was already six minutes into a 6h42m run.

**Current `main` already gates this run correctly.** What it does *not* do is make that answer visible, which is why diagnosing it took a 200-line structural reconstruction over 96k lines. This PR closes the three residual gaps.

One finding escalates #2136 and is worth recording: **no nested agent CLI ran here.** Codex executed `sed -n '1,1500p' /tmp/issue-905-research/direct-codex3.log` — it *read a stored log file*, two days old — and its own trace spliced that file's raw NDJSON into stderr. Any `cat`/`grep`/`head` of text that happens to contain NDJSON is enough. Both the `exec_command` and `exec` tool wrappers traced the same result, so one command echoed the payload twice.

## What changed

| Gap | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `log()` accepted `options.stream` and silently discarded it, so **all** mirrored agent output — both streams, all five tools — was written as `[INFO]` on our stdout | `log()` honours it: `[STDOUT]` / `[STDERR]` tags matching the stdio interceptor's existing vocabulary (#1549), and mirrored stderr now goes to our stderr so piping stdout yields only what the child wrote there. Explicit `level` still wins; callers passing no stream are unchanged. Swept across `codex`, `claude` (which passed an unrecognised `'raw'`), `gemini`, `opencode`, `qwen` |
| `codex exec` starts exactly one thread, so a `thread.started` with a different `thread_id` on the protocol stream is *proof* of echo — and that signal was going unused | Recorded as `state.foreignThreadIds` and reported: `🧬 Foreign thread IDs seen on the codex protocol stream (echoed, not codex sessions): …` |
| The failure reason carried counts and nothing else, so a false positive could not be refuted from the posted comment | The reason now also states the ordered turn lifecycle, how many `turn.started` were discarded as echoed telemetry, and any foreign thread id. `getCodexCompletionHealth` returns `turnLifecycle` / `echoedTurnStarts` / `foreignThreadIds` |

Housekeeping: `codex.lib.mjs` crossed the 1500-line ESLint budget, so the usage-field vocabulary and its JSON-path helpers moved to `src/codex.usage-fields.lib.mjs` (pure data + pure lookups, no behaviour change).

**No gate outcome changes.** A genuinely truncated turn (#1990) still fails; a completed run with echoed events still passes.

## How to reproduce

```bash
# 1. Recover stream provenance from the real incident log (both streams were tagged [INFO])
node experiments/issue-2140/classify-turn-events.mjs

# 2. Replay the rebuilt streams through the real parser + gate, three code versions
node experiments/issue-2140/replay-completion-gate.mjs
```

Output of (2), from the real log:

```
rebuilt streams — stdout: 4082 lines, stderr: 91895 lines
1. v2.11.7 — merged + count gate:            healthy false, turn.started=3, turn.completed=1, turn.failed=0
2. #2136 Layer B only — merged + order gate: healthy true
3. current main — separated + order gate:    healthy true, turn.started=1, turn.completed=1,
     echoed (stderr, ignored): unknown=68, thread.started=2, turn.started=2, item.completed=6, item.started=2
```

Line 1 reproduces the issue title verbatim. Every extra `turn.started` sits on stderr inside a `codex.tool_result` dump, next to a thread id that is not this session's.

## Tests

`tests/test-issue-2140-stream-provenance.mjs` — 21 assertions, fixtures copied verbatim from the incident log (`019fcaed-…` = real session, `019fc374-…` = echoed):

1. **Incident reproduction** — merged parse gives 3/1; split parse gives 1/1 with `telemetryEventCounts['turn.started'] === 2`; health is true; session id survives.
2. **`log()` provenance** — `[STDOUT]`/`[STDERR]` in the log file, console routing to stderr, explicit level wins, no-stream unchanged, plus a source scan asserting all five tool libs pass both stream names and none passes `'raw'`.
3. **Foreign thread detection** — recorded, deduped, session id untouched, absent on a clean run, surfaced in diagnostics.
4. **Gate self-explanation** — a genuine cut-off still fails; reasons carry the ordered lifecycle, the echoed count and the foreign id; a healthy run has no reasons but still exposes the fields.

## Case study

[`docs/case-studies/issue-2140/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-2140-7848faa1a777/docs/case-studies/issue-2140) — timeline with log line numbers, the full 96k-line run log (gzipped), PR/commit/check-run JSON proving the run succeeded, the requirements table (R1–R11), root-cause analysis, options considered and rejected, prior art, and the upstream update.

## Upstream

The upstream defect is RC4 from #2136, already filed as [openai/codex#36804](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36804) (unescaped multi-line `output=` in `codex_otel` tool-result records). This incident is not a separate upstream bug, so it is added as evidence on that issue rather than filed as a duplicate — but it strengthens it materially: no nested agent is required, and the dump is emitted twice. Minimal repro, workaround and code-level fix suggestions are in §7 of the case study.

Collects the raw data for the #2140 case study (the solve run log, the
GitHub state of the run's issue/PR/checks) and adds two experiments that
recover what actually happened:

- classify-turn-events.mjs recovers per-line stream provenance from the
  merged log (both streams are logged as [INFO], so it groups lines by
  the shared log() timestamp and classifies a chunk as stderr when it
  carries Codex OTEL tracing). Result: stdout carried exactly one
  thread.started/turn.started/turn.completed for the real session
  019fcaed-...; the two extra thread.started/turn.started pairs are on
  stderr, inside codex_otel codex.tool_result dumps, and belong to a
  foreign thread 019fc374-... .

- replay-completion-gate.mjs feeds those reconstructed streams through
  the parser and the completion gate. Merging the streams and applying
  the pre-#2136 count rule reproduces the issue title exactly
  (turn.started=3, turn.completed=1, turn.failed=0 -> unhealthy); either
  #2136 layer alone reports the run healthy.

Refs #2140

- log() accepted options.stream but ignored it, so every agent CLI's stderr
  was mirrored as [INFO] on our stdout. Provenance now shows as [STDOUT]/
  [STDERR], matching the existing stdio-interceptor tags, and mirrored stderr
  is written to our stderr.
- A thread.started announcing a thread id other than the session's is proof
  of echoed protocol; record it as state.foreignThreadIds and report it.
- The completion-failure reason now carries the ordered turn lifecycle, the
  echoed turn.started count and any foreign thread id, so a false positive
  is falsifiable from the posted comment alone.

Also splits the codex usage-field vocabulary into codex.usage-fields.lib.mjs
to stay within the max-lines budget.
